title: Learning to move as a rope team
summary: A first-time glacier team practiced travel systems, route planning and communication before taking on a guided training objective. The camp's main achievement was learning to make decisions together, not reaching a summit.
imageAlt: Roped climbers approaching a snowy mountain ridge

title: A steady pace in the high Andes
summary: A small training group used staged day hikes and pack carries to practice pacing, layering and team check-ins. Their final lesson was that a flexible plan and a well-timed turnaround are expedition skills too.
imageAlt: A mountain valley opening toward high peaks

title: Finding confidence on a hut-to-hut route
summary: Participants practiced map reading, weather checks and route alternatives while moving between mountain refuges. A stormy afternoon became an opportunity to revise the next day's plan and learn from local hut staff.
imageAlt: Mountain peaks under a clear evening sky

title: One team, different paces
summary: The group focused on gradual altitude gain, rest and regular wellbeing checks. Participants supported one another through a deliberately measured itinerary, with the guides adjusting the plan as conditions and individual needs changed.

title: Winter skills and careful choices
summary: A winter skills group reviewed snow travel, cold-weather systems and avalanche bulletins with local instructors. When the forecast narrowed their options, the team chose a lower-risk training day and returned with useful practice.

title: A weather window shared well
summary: A small team used a clear weather window for coached movement on alpine terrain, keeping a backup objective ready. Shared route checks and a conservative descent plan made the day a valuable skills milestone.
imageAlt: Alpine ridgelines beyond a broad mountain valley
